title: Hammer Candle Explained: A Real Bitcoin Example
text: This one candle can warn you that a fall may be ending. Traders call it the hammer. It has a small body near the top. Its lower wick is long, at least 2 times the body. That wick means sellers pushed the price down hard. But buyers pushed it back up before the candle closed. So the buyers won this battle. A hammer matters most at the end of a downtrend. Here is a real Bitcoin candle from September 28. It fell to 82,562 dollars. Then it closed at 83,068 dollars. Small body on top, long lower wick: a real hammer. 5 candles later, Bitcoin was 1 percent higher. Wait for the next candle to close higher. That is confirmation. Put your stop loss just below the wick. A hammer is a clue, never a promise. Watch live whale moves for free on MarketRadar Whale.
